title: A hidden tax-return section left 59 businesses waiting for refunds

beats.text: A business could pay this tax in advance and still owe nothing at year end.

visual.sub: Estimated payments followed the prior year’s tax

beats.text: Estimated payments followed the prior year, before pandemic receipts fell.

visual.kicker: Estimated payments followed the prior year’s tax

beats.text: The historical threshold was $50 million in taxable receipts.

visual.label: Estimated payments followed the prior year’s tax

beats.text: The online return displayed the tax section only above $50 million.

visual.kicker: The online return hid the tax section below the threshold

beats.text: That made the form simpler for most filers.

visual.line: A simpler form for most businesses

beats.text: It also missed businesses that had already paid and needed a refund.

visual.kicker: The online return hid the tax section below the threshold

beats.text: Disaster service assignments delayed the usual compliance checks.
The analyst identified 59 businesses and estimated $2.7 million in principal.

visual.label: The usual authorization window had closed

beats.text: The one-year window had already closed, so the Board passed a special ordinance.

visual.kicker: The Board authorized refunds through April 30, 2023

beats.text: It allowed refunds through April 2023 for qualified filers.
A payment register would tell us how much actually reached those businesses.
Every source is linked in the case file below.
